meta.title: Houssem Ben Hassen - Frontend Technical Lead
meta.description: Frontend Technical Lead with 8+ years of experience architecting large-scale web applications, leading engineering teams, and expanding into AI engineering.

hero.name: Houssem Ben Hassen
hero.headline: Frontend Technical Lead for teams building products that scale.
hero.subtext: 8+ years architecting frontend systems, leading engineering teams, and shipping resilient products. Currently expanding into AI engineering.

about.heading: About
paragraphs: My path into software started with embedded systems: sensors, microcontrollers, and the kind of programming where a wasted cycle actually matters. That discipline carried over when I moved to the web, and it still shapes how I build today.

Over the past 8+ years, I've grown from writing frontend code to leading it: designing micro-frontend architectures, setting up the CI/CD pipelines that ship them, and mentoring the developers who maintain them. I'm just as comfortable in a Node.js service or a PostgreSQL schema as I am in a component library, which makes me a useful bridge between frontend and backend teams rather than a specialist who only sees half the system.
I'm currently applying that same systems-first curiosity to AI engineering: agents, retrieval, and the tooling that makes developers faster, not just the frontend that sits on top of it.

experience.heading: Experience
experience.subheading: Eight years, five companies, one throughline: frontend systems built to last.

roles.title: Frontend Technical Lead
roles.summary: Leading frontend architecture for VMS, iObeya's newest product, and setting technical direction for the team that builds it.
achievements: Designed and led the adoption of a micro-frontend architecture for VMS, letting feature teams ship independently without stepping on each other's code.
Built and shipped an internal Vue.js component library, giving product teams a consistent, reusable UI foundation.
Replaced ad-hoc event handling with a centralized, finite-state-machine-driven event system, making complex UI state predictable and easier to debug.
Set up GitLab CI pipelines automating deployment and static code analysis, removing manual steps from every release.
Run code reviews and mentor junior developers, raising the team's baseline for code quality and architectural judgment.

roles.title: Senior Frontend Developer
roles.summary: Joined iObeya to work on the frontend of its core visual management and collaboration product.
achievements: Built and maintained core frontend features for iObeya's visual collaboration platform using Vue and Vuex.
Covered critical UI logic with Jest and used XState to manage complex interaction states.
Worked with AWS Cognito and S3 for authentication and asset storage.

roles.title: Frontend Developer
roles.summary: Delivered frontend for two products end to end, from early build-out through to production.
achievements: Built the frontend of a trading platform using React, Redux, and Material UI, integrated with AWS Cognito and S3.
Developed the frontend for izi-place, a web marketplace application, with React, Redux, and Material UI.
Worked with Node.js and MongoDB across the stack where backend support was needed.

roles.title: Fullstack Web Developer
roles.summary: Contributed frontend and backend work to Paytea, an HR and payroll management platform.
achievements: Built the frontend in React and Redux.
Developed backend services in Node.js using the Sails framework.
Built a recruitment flow with video capture and streaming, where candidate applications were submitted as recorded video.
Worked in a Scrum team with PostgreSQL as the primary datastore.

roles.title: Fullstack Web Developer
roles.summary: Built Taiga.voyage, a travel comparison product, end to end for a KyalisTech client.
achievements: Developed the frontend with React and Redux.
Built backend services in Node.js and designed the PostgreSQL data model.
Owned database analysis and schema decisions for the product.

roles.title: Fullstack Web Developer
roles.summary: Worked across the frontend and backend of jobi.tn, a recruitment platform, and its video-based application flow.
achievements: Contributed to frontend and backend development of the jobi.tn recruitment website.

projects.heading: Featured work
projects.subheading: A selection of products shipped across five companies and eight years.

items.solution: Designed and led the implementation of a micro-frontend architecture, paired with a shared Vue.js component library and a centralized, state-machine-driven event system.
highlights: Independent team ownership of feature domains
Reusable component library adopted across products
Centralized event handling via finite state machines

items.name: iObeya Visual Collaboration Platform
items.problem: The core iObeya product needed continued frontend development to support visual collaboration workflows for enterprise teams.
items.solution: Built and maintained frontend features with Vue and Vuex, covering critical UI logic with Jest and managing complex interactions with XState.

items.name: Trading Platform

items.solution: Delivered the platform's frontend in React, Redux, and Material UI, connected to AWS-backed authentication and storage.

items.name: Taiga.voyage

items.name: jobi.tn Recruitment Platform

architecture.heading: Architecture & engineering
architecture.subheading: What sets the work apart from frontend-only development.

pillars.name: Micro-frontend architecture
pillars.description: Designed and implemented micro-frontend architectures that let independent teams ship features without stepping on each other's code, most recently for iObeya's VMS product.

pillars.name: Component libraries
pillars.description: Built and maintained internal Vue.js component libraries, giving product teams a shared, consistent UI foundation instead of one-off implementations.

pillars.name: State management at scale
pillars.description: Replaced ad-hoc event handling with finite-state-machine-driven systems using XState, making complex UI behavior predictable, testable, and easier to reason about.

pillars.name: CI/CD & delivery
pillars.description: Set up GitLab CI pipelines automating deployment and static analysis, removing manual steps from the release process.

pillars.name: Full-stack fluency
pillars.description: Comfortable across the stack, from Node.js, Express, and Sails backends to PostgreSQL and MongoDB data models, which grounds frontend architecture decisions in how the whole system behaves.

pillars.name: Cloud & containers
pillars.description: Works with Docker, Kubernetes, and AWS (Cognito, S3) to deploy and operate the systems he architects.

pillars.name: Technical leadership
pillars.description: Runs code reviews, mentors junior developers, and leads sprint planning, treating team growth as part of the job rather than a side effect of it.

aiJourney.heading: AI engineering
aiJourney.headline: Expanding into AI engineering.
paragraphs: After years of building the systems developers and users interact with directly, I'm now applying the same engineering rigor to AI: how agents are built, how context is engineered, and how developer tools built on top of LLMs actually hold up in practice.
This is active, hands-on learning built on top of 8+ years of production engineering experience, not a pivot away from it.
